title: Louis Prima and Sidney Arodin records
summary: Allen shares favorite Louis Prima records and mentions clarinetist Sidney Arodin.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Okay, we thank you for calling. Let's talk it over. Gentlemen, what about another New Orleans musician? What about Louis Prima? Any comments? Dick Allen. I haven't heard much from Louis Prima lately. Of course, I collect old records, and I like the ones when he had people like Eddie Miller and George Brunis and Pee Wee Russell with him. Those happen to be my favorites. And some with, well, what do you call them? Monk Meyer? Gene Meyer?

Yeah. Gene Meyer. Some of those are, I believe Ray Benitez may be on some of them, too. Anyway, they're marvelous records. And once again, some of those have been reissued. Let's have a jubilee with Sidney Ayrton on clarinet. A fellow who rode up the Lazy River with Hoagy Carmichael. A forgotten figure today to most people, but one of the great New Orleans clarinet players. Okay, with that, let's go to the next line. Good morning. You're on with Dick Allen and Johnny Wiggs.
